title.value: QA your app and check failed deployments from your phone

introduction.value: A developer used Grok Bot to test their own app remotely and check failed deployments, and earlier to chase a A$17.49 refund via a website's live chat.

method.value: Lewis Cianci set up four Grok Bots, each with its own screen on a shared cloud computer, to work on his CheapMulch app. Two bots played an arborist and a requester and used the live site. A third bot fixed the code and pushed it. A fourth bot watched Dokploy and diagnosed a failed build. Testers confirmed each deploy by checking a commit-hash header.

outcome.value: The testers found confusing labels, a stuck map pin, a disabled Publish button and a date off by one. They missed overlapping text, which he spotted himself. He also had to remind the coding bot to switch to main.

notes.value: He used SuperGrok at US$30 a month, on a three-months-for-one deal. All bots share files, logins and deploy access, so prompt injection is a risk.

source_text.body:
QA your app and check failed deployments from your phone
A developer used Grok Bot to test their own app remotely and check failed deployments, and earlier to chase a A$17.49 refund via a website's live chat.
Done with
GB
Grok Bot
What they did
Lewis Cianci set up four Grok Bots, each with its own screen on a shared cloud computer, to work on his CheapMulch app. Two bots played an arborist and a requester and used the live site. A third bot fixed the code and pushed it. A fourth bot watched Dokploy and diagnosed a failed build. Testers confirmed each deploy by checking a commit-hash header.
How it went
The testers found confusing labels, a stuck map pin, a disabled Publish button and a date off by one. They missed overlapping text, which he spotted himself. He also had to remind the coding bot to switch to main.
Worth knowing
He used SuperGrok at US$30 a month, on a three-months-for-one deal. All bots share files, logins and deploy access, so prompt injection is a risk.
Try it yourself
with
Grok Bot
Copy prompt
Please QA my app at [app URL] by logging in with the test account [test login] and walking through these flows: [sign up, checkout, key features]. Also check [hosting or CI service, e.g. Vercel or GitHub Actions] for failed deployments in [project name] and read the logs. When you finish, send me a short report listing each bug you found with steps to reproduce it, plus the likely cause of any failed deployment. Do not redeploy, change settings, or submit any real payment without showing me first and getting my approval.
Original source: https://blog.logrocket.com/grok-bot-testing-friends/
